title: Competitor benchmark: eight public Polymarket insider-detection repositories (20 Nov 2026)

our_repository.name: searadacunha/Polymarket-Home-of-the-Insiders
our_repository.note: Every statement about this repository was re-read in a clone at this commit (origin/main on 20 Nov 2026, after the five monitoring changes of that day).

status_words: VERIFIED: read in the file at the pinned commit, or counted in the archived tree listing. REPORTED: stated by the project itself (README, comment, paper) and not recomputed here. NOT ASSESSED: no file of that repository was read for this capability; absence of a cell value is not evidence of absence.
result_text: The comparison is not audit grade for a ranking. The eight repositories were not chosen by frozen inclusion criteria: they came from a GitHub repository search and an earlier provisional card, so the set is open to a selection-bias challenge. No competitor code was executed; every competitor statement comes from files and metadata read through the public GitHub API at the pinned commits.

No first-place claim is made. The weaknesses listed below are the reasons: the main one is that this repository's own frozen detection study is negative (NOT_SUPPORTED), and an auditor will not rank a detector first on a negative result.

capabilities.name: Collection and indexing
capabilities.basis: Every compared repository collects its own data; ours reads chain logs, others read APIs, archives or a private database. No one collector is clearly ahead on the evidence read.

ours.value: A live collector of Polygon OrderFilled logs, and a live engine that keeps fills, Gamma markets and deposit receipts in one SQLite file

veeradittya/polymarket-insider-detection.value: Case-filtered, resumable GDELT GKG ingestion that records each file's sha1; trades from bulk archives

vsbtc/polymarket-insider-detection.value: One-shot collection of markets and trades from public APIs

pselamy/polymarket-insider-tracker.value: Live polling ingestor with health metrics

orcalayer/polymarket-insider-score-backt.value: Private database; the public script needs a paid API key

yasithdsl/polymarket-surveillance.value: Data loader for a backtesting harness

capabilities.name: Fill decoding
capabilities.basis: Ours decodes V1 and V2 OrderFilled logs and cites tx, log index and block for each fill; the four repositories read for this use API rows, bulk archives or private data.

veeradittya/polymarket-insider-detection.value: Bulk trade archives; no log decoding seen

capabilities.name: Position and PnL reconstruction
capabilities.basis: No PnL code of the eight was read. Outside the set, the scout read a conversion-aware lot ledger with an on-chain balance check (NeomarketExplorer, below) that goes further than our case-scoped ledger.

ours.value: Case-scoped ledger: cash identity over Data API activity (TRADE, REDEEM), checked against on-chain pUSD mint and burn logs and the wallet balance; no MERGE, SPLIT or conversion handling found in it

BRKME/Polymarket_insider.value: A 'Mark-to-Market (open positions)' workflow for its own bets, not a forensic reconstruction

capabilities.name: Funding tracing depth
capabilities.basis: Case notes trace funding trees far deeper than any competitor read. The live engine stays inside the deposit receipt plus one predecessor, while pselamy's live profiler walks up to 3 hops (with a 44-hour window and no use in its score).

ours.value: Live engine: payer read inside the deposit receipt, with a unique same-token earlier-log path through at most 6 pass-through contracts and ambiguous joins left unresolved; one funding predecessor checked at its own block. Case notes: multi-hop trees (links_multihop.py to depth 3, EXPLORATORY; Railgun and Relay trees in the financial-links replay)

Benja-Pauls/polymarket-insider-detection.value: One case script: 50,000 blocks back from the chain tip in 5,000-block chunks

capabilities.name: Cross-chain exit tracing
capabilities.basis: Ours decodes and traces bridged exits with tested decoders; none of the funding-focused repositories read (vsbtc, pselamy, Benja-Pauls) traces exits in the files read. Four repositories were not assessed.

capabilities.name: Point-in-time discipline
capabilities.basis: Two competitors read funding state at run time or from the chain tip (verified defects). Ours reads history strictly before t and, since 20 Nov, pins payer code and nonce to the deposit block. Residual look-ahead: public tags are still read when the alert is built.

ours.value: asof.view reads rows dated strictly before t. Since 20 Nov: payer code and nonce read at the deposit block with no latest fallback, links used only with receipt_guard_v1 provenance, C4/C5 fan-out counted from links dated before the entry. Public tags are still read when the alert is built (data_quality.payer_tags)

repos.name: vsbtc/polymarket-insider-detection
repos.what_it_does: A one-commit batch pipeline: markets and trades from public APIs, a score and ranking of 7,784 wallets, a Poisson-binomial luck p-value, and each wallet's first USDC funder on Polygon through the Etherscan V2 API. One 6-wallet ring is hand coded.

strengths.text: wallet_rankings.csv has 7,784 rows with components s_calib, s_conc, s_fresh, s_chain and s_exit
Inflows of USDC.e and native USDC; a funder counts as a service when it pays 50 or more distinct recipients (SERVICE_RECIPIENTS=50, line 29; funder_fanout, lines 48-60)
luck_pvalue: an exact O(n^2) Poisson-binomial dynamic programme over entry prices (lines 26-47)
ring_funding_edges.csv: 8 edges with a test_then_send flag

defects.text: Funding is first funder only, one hop: usdc_inflows reads the first page of 300 transfers per token and funder_fanout stops at 10,000 transfers (lines 36-60)
The fan-out count is read at run time, not as of the bet (no timestamp filter in funder_fanout)
Needs an Etherscan API key (line 18); whether the free tier still covers Polygon is unknown
ring_trace.py hard codes 2 funders and 4 fresh wallets (lines 19-30)
One commit, no tests, no CI

better_than_us.text: Publishes a population ranking of 7,784 scored wallets. Ours: the frozen study publishes 45 alerts over 34,413 markets and no wallet ranking

Counts a funder's fan-out over its on-chain transfers (up to 10,000). Ours counts fan-out only over the wallets the live engine itself has linked (FANOUT_MAX 10, enrich.py), so a busy funder that the engine has seen pay few wallets is not excluded by that rule (the block-pinned nonce rule BUSY_NONCE 1,000 still applies)

we_do_better.text: Point-in-time: asof.view reads only rows dated before t, and since 20 Nov payer code and nonce are read at the deposit block; vsbtc reads fan-out at run time

The payer is read inside the deposit transaction across USDC, USDC.e and pUSD, wrapping and pass-through included, and equal-amount ties are refused rather than resolved to the first sender; vsbtc takes the first inbound transfer
Multi-hop tracing to depth 3 with a stated service rule (WINDOW 10,000 blocks, service = code, tag or 1,000 or more transactions, FANOUT_MAX 10), labelled EXPLORATORY

earlier_card_errors: The earlier card said our deep tracer is tied to case folders. Partly wrong: the deposit-payer reader is a generic function of the live engine; only the multi-hop tracer is study scoped.

our_side_corrections.text: The earlier card said the live engine has no fan-out rule and that the fan-out rule exists only in the EXPLORATORY links_multihop.py. Wrong: the live engine has FANOUT_MAX = 10 (enrich.py line 21, present since the engine was added on 14 Nov), counted over the engine's own stored links dated before the entry, and a block-pinned nonce rule (BUSY_NONCE 1,000). What is true: it does not count a funder's on-chain fan-out.

The earlier card listed a self-disclosed look-ahead in which payer tags and transaction counts are read when the alert is built. Since 20 Nov transaction counts and contract code are read at the deposit block, and unavailable historical state stays unresolved; public tags are still read when the alert is built and are used only to exclude services.

Since 20 Nov the live engine refuses ambiguous equal-amount receipt joins (unique same-token earlier-log path required) and excludes funding links cached before these guards from new C4/C5 alerts. This can lower C4/C5 coverage; no prospective comparison has measured precision.
The earlier card counted 51 monitoring tests. On 20 Nov at 0b0882c the count is 88, all passing.
The earlier list of French-language files outside sources/ named 16 paths; the heuristic list has 17 (research_notes/independent-forensic-audit-2026-11-08/REPORT.md was omitted).

method: Selection: the eight repositories are those of an earlier provisional card, built from a GitHub repository search for Polymarket insider-detection projects; they were not chosen by frozen inclusion criteria. The scout then screened 625 repositories from repository search (586 after removing the registry of external work (pull request 97), the eight, our own mentions and archived repositories) and arXiv; it did not use code search.

Reading: for each of the eight, the head commit, the recursive tree, the licence endpoint and the files cited were fetched through the public GitHub REST API on 20 Nov 2026 and read at the pinned commit. The compact metadata (heads, tree listings with blob sizes, licence results, BRKME workflow runs and compare result) is in raw/github_api_metadata.json; no third-party file content is committed.
Our side: every statement about this repository was re-read in a clone at 0b0882c, after the five monitoring changes of 20 Nov; the test counts come from running the four suites that day.
Not executed: no competitor code, test suite or pipeline was run. Their numbers are VERIFIED only when read or counted in their files, otherwise REPORTED.

Positions: a capability is 'ahead' or 'behind' when files read on both sides show it; 'mixed' when this repository is ahead on one part and behind on another; 'level' when no side is clearly ahead; 'not compared' when no competitor file for it was read. No numeric score was assigned.
not_shown: No competitor score, rank or weighted total: the earlier numeric card scores were neither re-scored nor endorsed.
No third-party code, data file or licence text is reproduced; licences marked none mean all rights reserved.
Files not opened: veeradittya's scan output and Leiden results, yasithdsl's test bodies, matthewmurden's C++ sources, BRKME's journals, pselamy's mutation workflow body and recall test.
The scout's eight projects and eight papers were read by the scout only; their tree listings are not archived here, so their paths are not checked by verify.py.
limits: The set of repositories is not exhaustive and was not fixed in advance, so no ranking follows from it.
Cells marked Not assessed say nothing about the competitor; several 'ahead' positions rest on the competitors that were read for that capability.
Whether the Etherscan V2 free tier still covers Polygon (vsbtc's dependency) is unknown.
The French-language count is a word-frequency heuristic (more than 5 hits of common French words), not a language classifier.
Paper findings are abstract level and were not rechecked.
This note's own verify.py is not yet called by the CI workflow.
